rows.answer: Michael Collins stayed in the command module Columbia during the Apollo 11 landing [[michael-collins]] «[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing». North American Aviation was the prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module [[north-american-aviation]] «[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module».

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
Before launch, the heaters of oxygen tank No. 2 were run on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] «[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours»

The Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] «[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2» The board's report pointed to the thermostatic switches. It called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] «[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share»

The switches were built for 28 volts, and the heater specification was later revised to 65 volts without changing them. [[oxygen-tank-2]] «[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed»

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The astronaut who caught German measles was Charlie Duke. The crew swap he set off brought in Jack Swigert, who replaced Ken Mattingly as Apollo 13 command module pilot.

Swigert did not win an office that he held. He was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982, but he died before taking office. [[jack-swigert]] «[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office»

The swap: [[charlie-duke]] «[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch». The swap was decided and announced on 1970-04-10. [[rubella-crew-swap]] «[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10»

The notes do not say how Swigert died.

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The "mailbox" was an improvised CO2 scrubber adapter, and the crew built it from radioed instructions.

- It was made from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape: [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] «[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape»
- The crew built it from radioed instructions: [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] «[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions»
- It was needed because the command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round: [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] «[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round»

The notes don't say how the crew assembled it step by step. The note also links the adapter to [[mission-control-houston]] as its designer, but no fact line states that, so I can't cite it.

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Apollo 13 dates in the brain, in order:

1. **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] «[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity»

2. **1970-04-10:** A KSC management meeting decided the crew swap, which was announced at a press conference. Ken Mattingly was removed as command module pilot and Jack Swigert took his place. [[rubella-crew-swap]] «[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10» · [[apollo-13]] «[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting)» · [[ken-mattingly]] «[stated] Assigned to Apollo 16 as command module pilot (was Apollo 13 command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting)»

3. **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] «[stated] Launched 1970-04-11»

4. **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded about 56 hours into the flight. The same day, a Mission Control abort decision changed the mission goal from a Fra Mauro lunar landing to a safe return to Earth. [[oxygen-tank-2]] «[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight» · [[apollo-13]] «[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision)»

5. **1970-04-17:** The crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down. [[apollo-13]] «[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17»

6. **June 1970 (no day recorded):** The Apollo 13 Review Board report was published. The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] «[stated] Published in June 1970» · [[apollo-13-review-board]] «[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2»
